result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_node_connectivity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute global node connectivity. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L53202-L53256){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_node_connectivity() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Node connectivity](/assets/graphs/get-node-connectivity.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two diamonds that share the hub node D, drawn in the accent color. Removing D alone disconnects the graph, so the node connectivity is 1, smaller than the edge connectivity of 2. The card shows the cut D and the value 1." width="100%"} Returns the minimum number of nodes whose removal disconnects the graph. This is computed as the minimum pairwise node connectivity over all pairs of non-adjacent nodes. Uses Menger's theorem: node connectivity equals the maximum number of node-disjoint paths. Implementation transforms the problem to max-flow. Time complexity: `O(V^4)` for complete enumeration of pairs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Minimum number of nodes needed to disconnect the graph. Returns `0` if already disconnected. Returns `n-1` for complete graph `K_n`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A cycle graph needs at least 2 nodes removed to disconnect it, since every node has exactly two neighbors offering alternate paths: ::: {#8b06a718 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() n = 6 for i in range(1, n + 1): graph.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(1, n + 1): graph.add_edge(str(i), str((i % n) + 1)) # Returns 2 graph.get_node_connectivity() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: A complete graph `K_5` is maximally connected: you'd need to remove all but one of the other 4 nodes to isolate any node: ::: {#caaa43da .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(1, 6): graph.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(1, 6): for j in range(i + 1, 6): graph.add_edge(str(i), str(j)) # Returns 4 graph.get_node_connectivity() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 4 ``` ::: :::
